candidates.exact_span: EPA-approved test procedures (methods) for the analysis and quantification of pollutants or pollutant parameters, including for the purposes of compliance monitoring/DMR reporting, permit renewal applications, or any other reporting that may be required as a condition of this permit, shall be sufficiently sensitive.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether analytical methods must be 'sufficiently sensitive' for compliance monitoring/DMR reporting affects which measurements can be treated as enforceable limit comparisons (A) and whether method-sensitivity requirements are part of applicable monitoring obligations (B).

candidates.exact_span: A method is "sufficiently sensitive" when (1) the method minimum level (ML) of quantification is at or below the level of the applicable effluent limit for the measured pollutant or pollutant parameter; or (2) if there is no EPA-approved analytical method with a published ML at or below the effluent limit (see table below), then the method has the lowest published ML (is the most sensitive) of the analytical methods approved under 40 CFR Part 136 or required under 40 CFR Chapter I, Subchapters N or 0, for the measured pollutant or pollutant parameter; or (3) the method is specified in this permit or has been otherwise approved in writing by the permitting authority (EPA Region 6) for the measured pollutant or pollutant parameter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different interpretations of which branch of the three-part sensitivity test applies, what counts as the 'applicable effluent limit,' or which CFR-approved methods qualify, would change the ML threshold used for a parameter and therefore whether a reported value can be compared to the effluent limit (A) and how sub-ML or non-quantified results are classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: The Permittee has the option of developing and submitting a report to justify the use of matrix or sample-specific MLs rather than the published levels. Upon written approval by EPA Region 6 the matrix or sample-specific MLs may be utilized by the Permittee for all future Discharge Monitoring Report (DMR) reporting requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether matrix or sample-specific MLs were approved in writing changes the quantification threshold governing DMR reporting and compliance comparison for affected parameters, altering limit-exceedance determinations (A) and the semantics of results reported against alternate MLs (C).

candidates.exact_span: Current EPA Region 6 minimum quantification levels (MQLs) for reporting and compliance are provided in Appendix A of Part II of this permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The Appendix A MQL values are needed to determine the operative quantification threshold for each parameter; different readings of which MQL applies, or whether Appendix A values supersede the general sensitivity rule, would change enforceable limit comparisons (A), method requirements tied to reporting (B), and classification of results below MQL (C).

candidates.computation_change_reason: This qualifier determines whether sensitivity condition (2) rather than condition (1) applies to listed pollutants; interpreting 'if specified' or whether a given parameter is covered shifts the ML standard used and therefore limit comparability and missing-data treatment for those parameters.
